claim.why_it_matters: Table 18 prints Numeric-edited with no category of its own and splits it into '— if usage is display' -> Alphanumeric and '— if usage is national' -> National. The markdown merges the two sub-rows into one line and drops the blank, so the lines pair positionally as Numeric-edited -> Alphanumeric and the merged usage line -> National: the category of HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE/QUOTE moved to a numeric-edited item of usage national reads as Alphanumeric.

verdict.reasoning:
The 300-dpi render of PDF page 503 (printed page 481), Table 18, HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE/QUOTE row: the receiving-operand column prints nine lines (Alphabetic, Alphanumeric, Alphanumeric-edited, National, National-edited, Numeric, Numeric-edited, '— if usage is display', '— if usage is national'). The figurative-constant column prints Alphanumeric x3, National x2, Alphanumeric, then a BLANK line opposite Numeric-edited, then Alphanumeric (display) and National (national). Markdown line 9 of page-503.md has 8
-separated entries per column: the two usage sub-rows are merged into one entry and the blank is dropped, so positional pairing gives Numeric-edited -> Alphanumeric and the merged usage entry -> National. The national-usage numeric-edited case loses its distinct category (National), which is a normative MOVE semantics change. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
